name: Collect specimens at a collection centre
summary: After registration a lab assistant calls the patient to a collection room, confirms identity with two identifiers, draws blood into the ordered tubes in a set order, labels them at the chair and collects or receives urine and other specimens. Serum tubes are clotted and spun in the centre, then everything is stored at the right temperature, bagged to dangerous goods rules and handed to the courier at the next pickup. Hard-to-find veins, fainting, haemolysed or underfilled tubes and labelling slips are the main problems, and the wait for the next courier run makes up most of the elapsed time.

baseline.org_archetype: A large private community laboratory company with about 200 collection centres of one to six chairs, staffed by lab assistants (Ontario), auxiliary nurses (Quebec) and technicians (Manitoba), with courier pickups several times a day.
baseline.notes: In 2020-2022 centres added screening questions, masks and cleaning between patients for COVID-19, which lengthened each collection slightly.

trigger: A registered patient with printed labels is waiting in the collection queue.
end_state: The specimens are labelled, processed, stored and handed to the courier, or no specimen could be collected.

volume.seasonality: Weekday mornings are busiest; summer and late December are quieter; spring 2020 volumes fell sharply.

evidence.note: Same as registration: org file process map and demand driver d_psc_visits.

Org file role and cost (Job Bank 33101 Ontario times 1.35). FTE estimate: about 46% of the 400 Ontario lab assistants' time, leaving room for registration and workplace drug test collections within the headcount. Assigned to all shared collection steps; see assumptions.
Org file role and cost; Quebec centres do about 17% of collections. Same steps as Ontario; FTE in proportion to visits.
Org file role and cost; Manitoba centres do about 12% of collections. FTE in proportion to visits.

steps.name: Call the patient to a collection room
steps.description: When a chair is free the lab assistant takes the next set of labels from the collection tray, calls the patient by first name or number and walks them to the collection room or cubicle.

error.defect_description: Wrong patient called for the set of labels.

evidence.note: Second wait after registration; queue waits of a few minutes (cureus23: 6.5 minutes mean; yoshimoto20: under 10 minutes for 90%); longer at morning peaks. Range is an estimate.

steps.name: Confirm identity and match the labels at the chair
steps.description: The lab assistant asks the patient to state their full name and date of birth and compares the answer with the labels and the requisition before touching a tube. A mismatch stops the collection until it is fixed.

error.defect_description: Identity check skipped or done against the wrong labels.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics) and CLSI GP41: positive patient identification with two identifiers at the point of collection

next.condition: labels or requisition do not match the patient

evidence.note: Name and date of birth matched against the requisition (uams_venip). Mismatch share is an estimate.

steps.name: Fix a label or order mismatch with the front counter
steps.description: The lab assistant takes the labels back to the registration counter, where the visit is corrected or the right labels are found and reprinted, and the identity check is repeated. Wrong labels are destroyed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Check preparation and safety questions, then glove up
steps.description: The lab assistant confirms fasting where needed, asks about latex or antiseptic allergy, fainting history, bleeding problems and arm restrictions such as a mastectomy side, then cleans hands and puts on gloves.

error.defect_description: Fasting status or arm restriction missed.

control.basis: CLSI GP41 venipuncture procedure and infection prevention practice (hand hygiene and gloves) required under ISO 15189 Plus

evidence.note: Standard steps of the GP41 and WHO procedures; times are estimates.

steps.name: Assemble tubes and supplies in order of draw
steps.description: The lab assistant picks the tube types on the tube list and lines them up in the order of draw, with a safety needle or butterfly set, holder, alcohol swab, gauze and bandage within reach.

error.defect_description: Wrong tube type picked or tube missing.

evidence.note: Order of draw from uams_venip; time estimate.

steps.name: Apply the tourniquet and prepare the site
steps.description: The lab assistant applies the tourniquet a few inches above the site, feels for a suitable vein in the antecubital area, cleans the site with alcohol and lets it dry, keeping the tourniquet on for under one minute.

error.defect_description: Tourniquet left on too long or site not dry, raising haemolysis risk.

control.basis: CLSI GP41: tourniquet time under 1 minute, site cleansed and air dried

evidence.note: Tourniquet limit from uams_venip; time estimate.

steps.name: Draw blood into the tubes in order of draw
steps.description: The lab assistant anchors the vein, inserts the needle, fills each tube in order of draw, releases the tourniquet once blood flows and inverts each tube the set number of times. Most draws fill two to five tubes.

error.defect_description: Haemolysed, clotted or underfilled tube.

evidence.note: Phlebotomy procedure 2.2 minutes mean (cureus23); 97% first-attempt success (Leung, in epmc_waittime); haemolysis flagged in 3.5% of outpatient serum specimens (tian22), most mild and not rejected; syncope 0.004% (yoshimoto20) with near-fainting more common. Shares are set from these.

steps.name: Make a second attempt
steps.description: After an unsuccessful first stick the lab assistant releases the tourniquet, removes the needle, chooses another site or a butterfly set on the hand, and tries once more with fresh supplies.

error.defect_description: Haemolysis or underfill from a difficult draw.

control.basis: CLSI GP41 and company procedure: no more than two attempts by one collector

evidence.note: Two-attempt rule from uams_venip; success share is an estimate.

steps.name: A team lead or second collector makes a final attempt
steps.description: The lab assistant asks the team lead or the most experienced colleague on shift to try. If that attempt also fails the patient is offered another day, advised to drink water, or referred back to the clinician.

error.defect_description: Haemolysis or underfill from a difficult draw.

control.basis: Company collection procedure: escalate after two unsuccessful attempts

next.condition: no blood obtained; patient to return or see clinician

evidence.note: Common practice; times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Manage a fainting or other reaction
steps.description: The lab assistant stops the draw, removes the needle, lowers the patient's head or reclines the chair, calls a colleague, gives water and watches the patient until recovered. Emergency services are called for a serious reaction.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Syncope incidence from yoshimoto20; first aid steps are common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Remove the needle, bandage and discard the sharp
steps.description: The lab assistant places gauze, withdraws the needle, activates the safety device and drops the needle and holder straight into the sharps container, then asks the patient to press for two minutes and applies a bandage.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act, Needle Safety regulation (O. Reg. 474/07): safety-engineered needles in laboratories and specimen collection centres; immediate sharps disposal

evidence.note: Pressure and disposal steps from uams_venip; needlestick share derived from about 21.6 sharps injuries per 1,000 FTE a year in medical practices (epmc_needle) against roughly 1,000 collections per person a month. The regulation is named from general knowledge and was not opened.

steps.name: Handle and report a needlestick injury
steps.description: The injured lab assistant washes the wound and tells the team lead, who arranges assessment at a hospital emergency department within hours, records the source patient, files the incident report and the compensation board form, and covers the station.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Ontario Workplace Safety and Insurance Act reporting of workplace injuries; company bloodborne pathogen exposure procedure

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Label the tubes at the chair
steps.description: With the patient still seated the lab assistant sticks a barcode label on each tube straight along the tube, writes initials and collection time, and asks the patient to confirm the name on the label.

error.defect_description: Tube labelled with another patient's label or left unlabelled.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus and CLSI GP41: specimens labelled at the point of collection in the presence of the patient

evidence.note: Labelling content from uams_venip. Identified mislabelling about 1.15 per 1,000 specimens in a hospital (epmc_mislabel), outpatient identification errors much lower; 0.1% per visit is set between these. Urine share is an estimate.

steps.name: Collect a urine or other specimen
steps.description: The lab assistant gives the patient a labelled container and instructions for a midstream sample, waits while the patient uses the washroom, receives the container, checks the lid and label and places it in a bag.

error.defect_description: Container leaks or label missing.

evidence.note: Common practice; the wait is the patient's time in the washroom while the assistant serves others.

steps.name: Receive a home-collected specimen
steps.description: The lab assistant takes a 24-hour urine jug, stool kit or other home-collected specimen, checks the patient label, collection times and container type against the order, records the total volume if needed and bags it.

error.defect_description: Wrong container, unlabelled or collection time missing.

evidence.note: Patients bring home-collected specimens their provider asked for (dyn_before); share and time are estimates.

steps.name: Record the collection in the LIS
steps.description: The lab assistant marks the order as collected, which records the collector, date and time, and enters the number of tubes, fasting status and any comment such as a difficult draw or a test not collected.

error.defect_description: Collection time or comment missing or wrong.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus traceability: identity of the collector and collection date and time recorded

evidence.note: Common practice; time estimate.

steps.name: Discharge the patient and clean the chair
steps.description: The lab assistant checks the puncture site has stopped bleeding, tells the patient how to get results, then wipes the chair arm and work surface, discards waste and restocks tubes for the next patient.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: serum or gel tube to spin

evidence.note: Common practice; share of visits with a serum or gel tube is an estimate.

steps.name: Load clotted tubes into the centrifuge
steps.description: Serum tubes wait in a rack until clotted, usually about 30 minutes. The lab assistant then balances them in the centrifuge with other patients' tubes and starts the run.

error.defect_description: Tube spun before clotting or unbalanced load.

control.basis: Tube manufacturer instructions and laboratory specimen requirements under ISO 15189 Plus: clotting time before centrifugation and separation within the stated limit

evidence.note: Clotting time of about 30 minutes is standard tube practice; batch wait and per-patient share of handling are estimates.

steps.name: Unload the centrifuge and check the spun tubes
steps.description: After the 10 to 15 minute run the lab assistant takes the tubes out, checks that the gel barrier formed and the serum looks clear, and notes any visibly haemolysed or lipaemic tube.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

steps.name: Aliquot or freeze specimens that need it
steps.description: For tests that need frozen or separated serum or plasma, the lab assistant pours or pipettes the serum into a labelled transport tube and puts it in the freezer or fridge.

error.defect_description: Aliquot mislabelled or wrong temperature.

evidence.note: Common practice; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Store specimens at the required temperature
steps.description: The lab assistant places each tube in the room temperature rack, refrigerator or freezer according to the test requirements and checks the temperature log for the fridge and freezer.

error.defect_description: Specimen stored at the wrong temperature.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus specimen handling and storage requirements (stability by test, monitored storage temperatures)

evidence.note: Common practice; time estimate.

steps.name: Bag the specimens for the courier
steps.description: Before each pickup the lab assistant puts each patient's tubes in a sealed biohazard bag with absorbent material and the requisition copy in the outer pocket, then groups bags by temperature in the marked transport box.

error.defect_description: Bag without requisition or specimen in the wrong temperature box.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations section 1.39 and Part 5: UN3373 Biological Substance, Category B in CGSB-43.125 Type P650 packaging with mark and 24-hour number

evidence.note: Packaging rule from tdg_regs; batch wait and per-patient time are estimates.

steps.name: Log the bags on the pickup manifest
steps.description: The lab assistant counts the bags in each temperature box, writes or prints the count on the pickup log or manifest for the courier and checks that no labelled specimen is left behind in the centrifuge or fridge.

error.defect_description: Count wrong or specimen left behind.

evidence.note: Common practice; time estimate.

steps.name: Hand the specimen boxes to the courier
steps.description: At the scheduled pickup the courier arrives, scans the stop and the boxes, and the lab assistant hands over the boxes and confirms the count. Specimens collected after the last pickup wait overnight in the fridge or at room temperature as their stability allows.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Pickups several times a day are standard for community collection centres. The wait range is an estimate net of the clotting and spinning time that runs in parallel, and includes specimens held until the next run.

steps.name: Count stock and place a supply order
steps.description: When tubes, needles, containers or requisition forms run low, the lab assistant counts what is left against the par levels and submits a supply order to the warehouse for the next delivery.

error.defect_description: Item missed, leading to a stock-out before the next delivery.

evidence.note: Roughly one order a week per centre spread over visits; estimate.

steps.name: Team lead documents the incident and decides next steps
steps.description: The team lead checks on the patient, decides with them whether the draw can be completed after recovery or should be rebooked, and records the event in the incident log for the quality team.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus: adverse events and nonconformities recorded and reviewed

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

steps.name: Regional manager reviews a serious incident
steps.description: The regional manager reads the incident record, calls the patient or family if needed, checks the collector's competency record and decides on follow-up such as retraining or a report to the director.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company incident management procedure: manager review of serious patient incidents

evidence.note: Common practice; estimates.

exceptions.name: First venipuncture attempt fails
exceptions.description: No blood or a lost vein; the collector tries once more at another site.

exceptions.name: Two attempts fail
exceptions.description: The team lead or most experienced colleague makes a final attempt; about a quarter of these patients leave without a specimen.

exceptions.name: Fainting or other reaction
exceptions.description: The draw stops, the patient is cared for until recovered and the team lead records the incident; most draws are completed afterwards.

exceptions.name: Label or order mismatch at the chair
exceptions.description: The patient's answer does not match the labels, so the labels go back to the counter for correction.

exceptions.name: Urine or swab collection
exceptions.description: The patient provides a urine sample in the washroom or a swab is taken.

exceptions.name: Home-collected specimen
exceptions.description: A 24-hour urine or stool kit is checked and accepted.

exceptions.name: Needlestick injury
exceptions.description: The collector is injured by a used needle; first aid, hospital assessment and injury reports follow.

benchmarks.population: Community collection centres with pickups several times a day

evidence.note: No published benchmark found. Estimate: a few minutes in the queue, about 7 minutes with the patient, 30 minutes to clot and 12 to spin, then up to a few hours until the next courier run.
Procedure only; Canadian draws usually fill more tubes.
Leung et al. abstract.

benchmarks.population: University of Tokyo Hospital outpatient blood collection room, 677,956 draws

benchmarks.unit: share of outpatient fasting serum specimens

evidence.note: Includes mild haemolysis that is reported with a comment rather than rejected.
Occult mislabelling estimated at 3.17 per 1,000.

pain_points.description: Most elapsed time is the wait for the next courier run; afternoon specimens can sit for hours, and late ones wait overnight.

evidence.note: Estimate from pickup schedules.

pain_points.description: Difficult veins cause repeat sticks, escalation to the team lead and some patients leaving without a specimen.

evidence.note: Two-attempt rule and 97% first-attempt success.

pain_points.description: Haemolysed, clotted or underfilled tubes and labelling slips are only found at the laboratory, so the patient has to come back.

evidence.note: Haemolysis and mislabelling rates.

pain_points.description: Clotting and centrifuging in the centre ties up staff between patients during the morning rush.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

sources.title: Routine venipuncture guidelines
sources.publisher: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences, Clinical Laboratory
sources.supports: Outpatients are asked their name and date of birth, which must match the requisition; never leave the tourniquet on for over 1 minute; do not attempt a venipuncture more than twice and notify a supervisor if unsuccessful; follow the order of draw; invert additive tubes 4 to 10 times; patient applies pressure for at least 2 minutes; label all tubes with patient labels, initials, date and time.

sources.title: PRE02 Collection of Diagnostic Venous Blood Specimens, 8th edition (replaces GP41-Ed7, 2017)
sources.supports: Establishes criteria for venous blood specimen collection for laboratory testing as a stepwise model procedure for outpatient and inpatient collection; GP41-Ed7 (2017) was the edition in force in 2019-2022.

sources.title: WHO guidelines on drawing blood: best practices in phlebotomy
sources.supports: Recommended steps for safe phlebotomy; each step carries risks for patients (bruising) and health workers (needle-stick injuries, bloodborne infection) and affects specimen quality; clerical errors can be fatal.

sources.title: Analysis of vasovagal syncope in the blood collection room in patients undergoing phlebotomy
sources.supports: 27 vasovagal syncope cases in 677,956 outpatient phlebotomies (0.004%); 5 or more tubes raised the rate to 0.016%; waits were under 10 minutes for 90% or more of patients.

sources.title: The incidence rate and influence factors of hemolysis, lipemia, icterus in fasting serum biochemistry specimens
sources.supports: Haemolysis index flagged 3.84% of 501,612 fasting serum specimens; 3.54% of outpatient specimens; longer transfer time associated with more haemolysis.

sources.title: Assessment of the number of phlebotomists in a newly established sample collection center
sources.supports: Outpatient collection centre time study: queue wait mean 6.5 minutes, phlebotomy procedure mean 2.2 minutes (1,200 patients).

sources.title: Europe PMC abstracts: phlebotomy waiting and turnaround time studies, including Leung et al., Audit of phlebotomy turnaround time in a private hospital setting (2006)
sources.supports: Leung et al.: success rate at first phlebotomy attempt 97%; job completion 10.4 minutes per ward request. Yun et al. 2016: automated reception cut mean time from reception to phlebotomy from 5:45 to 2:42 minutes.

sources.title: Europe PMC abstracts: specimen labelling and identification error studies (Raymond et al. 2024; Ning et al. 2016; Sandhu et al. 2017)
sources.supports: Raymond et al.: identified mislabelling 1.15 per 1,000 specimens, with blood-type discrepancies suggesting 3.17 per 1,000 occult mislabels. Ning et al.: outpatient identification errors 0.0067% of specimens before barcode labelling, 0.0001% after. Sandhu et al.: standardized labelling protocols cut labelling errors by a median 72%.

sources.title: Europe PMC abstracts: sharps injury studies, including Dulon et al., Circumstances of percutaneous sharps injuries in German healthcare workers 2015-2024
sources.supports: Medical practices had 21.6 percutaneous sharps injuries per 1,000 full-time equivalents a year; blood collection needles were the devices most often involved; 43% related to disposal.

sources.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations (SOR/2001-286), full text
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Section 1.39: UN3373 Biological Substance, Category B is exempt from most documentation and labelling parts if the means of containment complies with Part 5 (CGSB-43.125 Type P650), shows the Category B mark, the shipping name and a 24-hour telephone number; Part 6 sets training certificate requirements.

sources.title: Wages: Medical Laboratory Technical Assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $17.95, median $26.25, high $36.00 (2023-2024).

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Collection centres differ in hours and blood-drawing chairs (for example six chairs in a North York centre, two in a small rural one); providers target serving 90% of patients within 30 or 40 minutes; specimen rejection rates of 0% to 4.4% in sampled hospital laboratories.

sources.title: Patients and individuals: Before my test
sources.supports: Patients bring home-collected specimens their provider asked for; fasting of 4, 8 or 10 to 12 hours applies to listed tests.

assumptions: Shared steps are assigned to the Ontario lab assistant role because Ontario has about 70% of centres and staff; Quebec auxiliary nurses and Manitoba technicians follow the same procedure. Their FTE is stated in proportion to visits.
The workflow starts when the registered patient joins the collection queue and ends when the courier takes the specimens. The courier's work is in the route pickup workflow.
Per-patient shares of batch work (centrifuge loading, bagging, manifests) are amortised as fractions of a minute per patient.

Mean staff hands-on time is about 7.4 minutes per collection. At 560,000 collections a month this implies about 530 FTE at 130 productive hours, against 287 FTE stated here. With registration the total exceeds the org file's 580 front-line centre staff, which suggests the org file's visit volume is high or its centre headcount low. The stated FTE stays within the org file's headcount.
The needlestick probability is set from injury rates per FTE, not per draw, and is very small per collection.
Recollection visits for specimens rejected by the laboratory are not modelled separately; they enter as ordinary registered visits.
Loaded costs come from the org file (hourly wage times 1.35).
